$comment: The knowledge base: books, articles and research worth reading. Add an entry to works and the page lists it; the front page's Knowledge base entry becomes a link as soon as the list is not empty. kind is book, article or research. argues and holds are our own assessment: what the work argues, and where it holds (and where it does not). Works are grouped under topics (topic matches an id in topics).
$readNote: Read by Erlend B. Moe (from his Goodreads shelf, the books relevant to the institute). 'argues' is a one-line description of each work's thesis where it is well established; 'holds' is left for our own judgement.

$example.title: The Guns of August
$example.author: Barbara W. Tuchman
$example.argues: One or two sentences on the work's argument.
$example.holds: One or two sentences on where it holds, and where it does not.

topics.en: Populism, the radical right and movements

works.title: How Dictatorships Work: Power, Personalization, and Collapse
works.author: Barbara Geddes, Joseph Wright and Erica Frantz
works.argues: Autocracies differ by who holds power — a party, the military or one person — and that difference shapes how they rule, how long they last and how they fall.

works.title: Backsliding: Democratic Regress in the Contemporary World
works.author: Stephan Haggard and Robert Kaufman
works.argues: Democracies erode from within: polarisation lets elected incumbents expand executive power step by step while keeping elections.

works.title: Democracy in America? What Has Gone Wrong and What We Can Do About It
works.author: Benjamin I. Page and Martin Gilens
works.argues: American policy follows the preferences of the affluent and organised interests far more closely than those of ordinary citizens.

works.title: Patterns of Democracy: Government Forms and Performance in Thirty-Six Countries
works.author: Arend Lijphart
works.argues: Consensus democracies, which share power, perform at least as well as majoritarian ones on governing and better on representation.

works.title: Polyarchy: Participation and Opposition
works.author: Robert A. Dahl
works.argues: Real democracies are polyarchies, defined by two dimensions: open contestation and inclusive participation.

works.title: The Concept of Representation
works.author: Hanna Fenichel Pitkin
works.argues: Representation means several distinct things — formal, descriptive, symbolic and substantive — and the substantive sense, acting in others' interest, is the core.

works.title: Democratic Deficit: Critical Citizens Revisited
works.author: Pippa Norris
works.argues: Support for democracy as an ideal has not collapsed; the gap is between citizens' rising expectations and their judgement of how democracy performs.

works.title: Democracy and the Politics of Electoral System Choice: Engineering Electoral Dominance
works.author: Amel Ahmed
works.argues: Electoral systems were chosen by established elites to contain the rising working-class parties, not to serve democratic ideals.

works.title: Determinants of Democratization: Explaining Regime Change in the World, 1972–2006
works.author: Jan Teorell

works.title: Democracy and Democratization in Comparative Perspective
works.author: Jørgen Møller and Svend-Erik Skaaning

works.title: Transitions from Authoritarian Rule: Latin America
works.author: Guillermo O'Donnell, Philippe C. Schmitter and Laurence Whitehead (eds.)

works.title: Non-Democratic Regimes
works.author: Paul Brooker

works.title: The Global Divergence of Democracies
works.author: Larry Diamond and Marc F. Plattner (eds.)

works.title: The Oxford Handbook of the Quality of Government
works.author: Andreas Bågenholm et al. (eds.)

works.title: Between-Election Democracy
works.author: Peter Esaiasson and Hanne Marthe Narud (eds.)

works.title: The Madisonian Turn: Political Parties and Parliamentary Democracy in Nordic Europe
works.author: Torbjörn Bergman and Kaare Strøm (eds.)

works.title: The Nordic Models in Political Science: Challenged, but Still Viable?
works.author: Oddbjørn Knutsen (ed.)

works.title: After the Mass Party: Continuity and Change in Political Parties and Representation in Norway
works.author: Elin Haugsgjerd Allern

works.title: The Oxford Handbook of Electoral Persuasion
works.author: Elizabeth Suhay, Bernard Grofman and Alexander H. Trechsel (eds.)

works.title: The Oxford Handbook of Gender and Politics
works.author: Georgina Waylen et al. (eds.)

works.title: Valg og politikk siden 1945
works.author: Johannes Bergh et al.

works.title: Stat, nasjon, klasse: Essays i politisk sosiologi
works.author: Stein Rokkan

works.title: Land, makt og følelser: Stats- og nasjonsbygging
works.author: Frank Aarebrot

works.title: The Political System of the European Union
works.author: Simon Hix

works.title: What Is Populism?
works.author: Jan-Werner Müller
works.argues: Populism is not just anti-elitism but a moralised claim that only the populist represents the real people, which makes it inherently anti-pluralist.

works.title: Populism: A Very Short Introduction
works.author: Cas Mudde and Cristóbal Rovira Kaltwasser
works.argues: Populism is a thin ideology dividing society into a pure people and a corrupt elite, attaching itself to left or right host ideologies.

works.title: Populism
works.author: Benjamin Moffitt

works.title: The Oxford Handbook of the Radical Right
works.author: Jens Rydgren (ed.)

works.title: Liberal Roots of Far Right Activism: The Anti-Islamic Movement in the 21st Century
works.author: Lars Erik Berntzen
works.argues: The anti-Islamic movement justifies itself in liberal terms — women's rights, gay rights, free speech — rather than through older far-right ideas.

works.title: Power in Movement: Social Movements and Contentious Politics
works.author: Sidney Tarrow
works.argues: Social movements emerge and spread when political opportunities open and activists can draw on known repertoires of contention.

works.title: The Hour of the Predator
works.author: Giuliano da Empoli

works.title: Seeing Like a State: How Certain Schemes to Improve the Human Condition Have Failed
works.author: James C. Scott
works.argues: Grand state schemes fail when they force complex societies into simplified, legible categories and override local, practical knowledge.

works.title: Exit, Voice, and Loyalty: Responses to Decline in Firms, Organizations, and States
works.author: Albert O. Hirschman
works.argues: Members of a declining organisation or state can leave or speak up; loyalty delays exit and makes voice more likely.

works.title: Society Against the State: Essays in Political Anthropology
works.author: Pierre Clastres
works.argues: Stateless societies are not undeveloped states: they actively organise themselves to prevent coercive power from forming.

works.title: Fritz Wedel Jarlsberg: Diplomat uten grenser
works.author: Per Arne Totland

works.title: The Wealth Effect: How the Great Expectations of the Middle Class Have Changed the Politics of Banking Crises
works.author: Jeffrey M. Chwieroth and Andrew Walter
works.argues: As middle classes came to own more financial wealth, they expected governments to protect it, making ever larger bank bailouts politically unavoidable.

works.title: How Markets Fail: The Logic of Economic Calamities
works.author: John Cassidy
works.argues: Faith in self-correcting markets blinded economists and policymakers to market failures, setting up the 2008 crisis.

works.title: How Will Capitalism End? Essays on a Failing System
works.author: Wolfgang Streeck
works.argues: Capitalism is decaying from its own contradictions — low growth, rising debt and inequality — with no successor system in sight.

works.title: Capitalism Unleashed: Finance, Globalization, and Welfare
works.author: Andrew Glyn
works.argues: Since the 1970s, finance and globalisation have shifted power from labour to capital and put the welfare state under pressure.

works.title: The Endless Crisis: How Monopoly-Finance Capital Produces Stagnation and Upheaval from the USA to China
works.author: John Bellamy Foster and Robert W. McChesney
works.argues: Mature capitalism tends towards stagnation, and financialisation has been the main offset — at the price of recurring crises.

works.title: The Great Financial Crisis: Causes and Consequences
works.author: John Bellamy Foster and Fred Magdoff

works.title: Stagnation and the Financial Explosion
works.author: Harry Magdoff and Paul M. Sweezy

works.title: Keynes Against Capitalism: His Economic Case for Liberal Socialism
works.author: James Crotty
works.argues: Keynes's own writings make the case not for managing capitalism but for replacing it with a liberal socialism under public control of investment.

works.title: Money and Government: The Past and Future of Economics
works.author: Robert Skidelsky
works.argues: Mainstream economics misunderstood money and the role of the state; active fiscal policy and a better theory of money are needed.

works.title: John Maynard Keynes, 1883–1946: Economist, Philosopher, Statesman
works.author: Robert Skidelsky

works.title: The State and the Economy Under Capitalism
works.author: Adam Przeworski

works.title: The Nature and Logic of Capitalism
works.author: Robert L. Heilbroner

works.title: Rationalizing Capitalist Democracy: The Cold War Origins of Rational Choice Liberalism
works.author: S. M. Amadae
works.argues: Rational choice theory grew out of Cold War defence research and remade liberal democratic theory around individual self-interest.

works.title: Leftism Reinvented: Western Parties from Socialism to Neoliberalism
works.author: Stephanie L. Mudge
works.argues: Left parties changed as their economic experts changed — from socialist theorists to Keynesians to market-oriented economists.

works.title: Economic Rationality
works.author: Stephen G. Engelmann

works.title: An Introduction to Macroeconomics: A Heterodox Approach to Economic Analysis
works.author: Louis-Philippe Rochon and Sergio Rossi (eds.)

works.title: The Three Worlds of Welfare Capitalism
works.author: Gøsta Esping-Andersen
works.argues: Welfare states cluster into three regimes — liberal, conservative and social democratic — that shape markets, families and class.

works.title: Poor Economics: A Radical Rethinking of the Way to Fight Global Poverty
works.author: Abhijit V. Banerjee and Esther Duflo
works.argues: Careful evidence on how poor people actually make decisions does more to fight poverty than grand theories for or against aid.

works.title: Understanding Poverty
works.author: Abhijit V. Banerjee, Roland Bénabou and Dilip Mookherjee (eds.)

works.title: Due Diligence: An Impertinent Inquiry into Microfinance
works.author: David Roodman
works.argues: Microfinance does little to lift people out of poverty; its real value lies in financial services and in building institutions.

works.title: Just Give Money to the Poor: The Development Revolution from the Global South
works.author: Joseph Hanlon, Armando Barrientos and David Hulme
works.argues: Regular cash transfers to poor households are one of the most effective and affordable development tools.

works.title: The Economics of Microfinance
works.author: Beatriz Armendáriz and Jonathan Morduch

works.title: Routledge Handbook of Indigenous Peoples in the Arctic
works.author: Timo Koivurova et al. (eds.)

works.title: The Routledge Handbook of the Polar Regions
works.author: Mark Nuttall, Torben R. Christensen and Martin J. Siegert (eds.)

works.title: Indigenous Peoples' Governance of Land and Protected Territories in the Arctic
works.author: Thora Martina Herrmann and Thibault Martin (eds.)

works.title: Northern Exposure: Peoples, Powers and Prospects in Canada's North
works.author: Frances Abele et al. (eds.)

works.title: Red Skin, White Masks: Rejecting the Colonial Politics of Recognition
works.author: Glen Sean Coulthard
works.argues: State recognition of Indigenous peoples reproduces colonial power; Indigenous resurgence on their own terms is the alternative.

works.title: First Nations? Second Thoughts
works.author: Tom Flanagan
works.argues: Claims to Indigenous self-government and special status in Canada rest on weak arguments and lead to poor outcomes.

works.title: From Treaty Peoples to Treaty Nation: A Road Map for All Canadians
works.author: Greg Poelzer and Ken S. Coates

works.title: The Other Side of Eden: Hunters, Farmers, and the Shaping of the World
works.author: Hugh Brody
works.argues: Hunter-gatherers are not an earlier stage of humanity; farming cultures are the restless, expansionist ones.

works.title: Indigenous Peoples: Self-determination, Knowledge, Indigeneity
works.author: Henry Minde (ed.)

works.title: Native Power: The Quest for Autonomy and Nationhood of Indigenous Peoples
works.author: Jens Brøsted et al. (eds.)

works.title: The Sámi People: Traditions in Transition
works.author: Veli-Pekka Lehtola

works.title: Multicultural Citizenship: A Liberal Theory of Minority Rights
works.author: Will Kymlicka
works.argues: Liberal principles can justify group-differentiated rights for national minorities and immigrant groups.

works.title: Contemporary Political Philosophy: An Introduction
works.author: Will Kymlicka

works.title: Why Not Socialism?
works.author: G. A. Cohen
works.argues: The equality and community of a shared camping trip show socialist ideals are desirable; the open question is feasibility.

works.title: Political Ideologies and the Democratic Ideal
works.author: Terence Ball and Richard Dagger

works.title: Rettferdig fordeling og rettferdig skatt
works.author: Jørgen Pedersen

works.title: The Oxford Handbook of Political Consumerism
works.author: Magnus Boström, Michele Micheletti and Peter Oosterveer (eds.)

works.title: The Politics of Volunteering
works.author: Nina Eliasoph
